_comment: Frozen contract for whether a message asks an agent for something, and why.
Three things act on the answer and must give the same one: the herdr
doorbell (a wake queued with the reason), `await` (the message handed over
as the agent's turn) and the wake digest (the message listed as asking for
the agent). The rule is fastapi-backend/app/services/asks.py:
Only chat asks: an exchange carrying a `message` or a `reply` with text.
Nobody asks themselves.
A mention asks: `mention`, or `interrupt` for @!. Not a mention of an
engine, which summons it, and nobody when the text summons a conductor,
since the members it names are bound to its roles and asked later.
A `message` asks its recipients: `turn`.
A `reply` asks only whoever it mentions; its recipient is whoever the
replier last heard from, which `respond` fills in.
Each case is one message, written the way its sender writes it, and one
agent. The cast: coder and planner are agents with herdr panes, hay is a
person posting from the app, aligner and conductor are engines of those
kinds, sage is a persona, builder is a worker, remote is an A2A agent.
`sender` posts `text` in the room or the task's thread (`where`). `to` is
who an engine's turn or an A2A answer is for, or who an agent last heard
from before it replied. `shape` names a signal or an engine turn when the
sender alone doesn't say. `asks` is the reason for `agent`, or null.
fastapi-backend/tests/test_wake_paths_table.py writes each case through
the route or engine call that sends it and asserts the doorbell, `await`,
the digest and asks() itself all give `asks`.
